protobuf-java (all versions): CVE-2026-0994 is a Python-only vulnerability in the protobuf library's json_format.ParseDict() function — a recursion- depth counter bug in Python's json_format.py. The Java implementation does not contain that code. NVD assigns the cross-language CPE cpe:/a:google:protobuf to this CVE, which Dependency-Check then incorrectly matches against the Java protobuf-java artifact. Fix versions cited in the CVE (5.29.6, 6.33.5) are Python package versions.
This rule matches any protobuf-java JAR by filename (so it survives version bumps) and suppresses only CVE-2026-0994. Future Python-only or C++-only CVEs that NVD assigns to cpe:/a:google:protobuf on the Java artifact will need their own entries — we tried broader matchers (<packageUrl> and version-agnostic <cpe> in both CPE 2.2 and 2.3 forms) in earlier commits on the IGDD-2928 branch and verified in publish runs 26310238352 and 26316297788 that neither shape produces a match in this project's Dependency-Check configuration. Root cause: the workflows pass --disableCentral, so 44 of 134 scanned JARs (protobuf-java among them) have no PURL identifier, and the <cpe> matcher's containment semantics did not connect our value (in either CPE form) to the vulnerability identifiers Dependency-Check emits. The narrower filePath + CVE pattern is documented in the Dependency-Check suppression guide and is the form known to work here. Added: 2026-05-22

CVE-2026-66908 is in the Apache Camel Platform HTTP Main component: the camel-main embedded HTTP server built JWTAuth from the keystore alone when neither jwtIssuer nor jwtAudience was set, so inbound tokens were checked only for signature and expiry (JWTAuthenticationConfigurer.buildJwtOptions, Vert.x JWTAuth). See CAMEL-24281.
That code is not on the classpath here. Verified on camel 4.18.4, in both the BOM validation tree and izgw-transform: - camel-platform-http-main : not resolved in either tree - io.vertx : not resolved in either tree - camel-main-4.18.4.jar : contains no JWT, platform-http or Vert.x classes izgw-transform is a Spring Boot application using camel-spring-boot-starter. It never starts camel-main's standalone HTTP server, and could not without Vert.x present. Dependency-Check matches on version alone: cpe:2.3:a:apache:camel:* covers "from 4.8.0 up to excluding 4.22.0" for every camel artifact, whatever the module.
There is no upgrade that clears this on our line. Per the advisory: "This behaviour is fixed only on 4.22.0 ... The fail-closed guard could not be backported. The jwtIssuer and jwtAudience options were themselves only introduced in 4.21.0 by CAMEL-23525, so on camel-4.18.x and camel-4.14.x there was nothing an operator could set to satisfy the requirement." 4.18.4 is the newest 4.18.x release, and camel 4.22.0 requires Spring Boot 4.1 / Spring Framework 7 while this BOM pins spring-boot.version on 3.5.x. The real remediation is the Spring Boot 4 plus Camel 4.22 upgrade. See versions-rules.xml for the cap that keeps automation on 4.18.x until then.
Matched on <cve> alone, with no dependency selector, so it applies wherever this one CVE is raised. Do not add <cpe>cpe:/a:apache:camel</cpe>: per the suppression XSD <cpe> is a suppress-what element, not a dependency selector, so it would hide every Camel finding including future ones.
WARNING - read before changing the date. This CVE is CVSS 7.5, at or above the --failOnCVSS 7 gate used by both dependency-updates.yml and publish.yml. When this suppression expires the scan fails hard: the nightly exits 1 with no PR, and publish.yml exits 1 so develop stops deploying to GitHub Packages. Recovery needs an edit to this file. CVE-2026-59283 (SpEL SimpleEvaluationContext safety-guard bypass) and CVE-2026-59313 (functional-web SSE stream corruption): verified not exploitable in izgw-hub, izgw-transform, izgw-core, or v2tofhir — none use SimpleEvaluationContext for SpEL, and none use Spring's functional RouterFunction/HandlerFunction web framework for SSE. No fix exists on the Spring Framework 6.2.x line; the real fix ships only in 7.0.9, which requires Spring Boot 4.x. Should clear once the Boot 4 upgrade lands. Expires 2027-02-28. Added: 2026-09-02

CVE-2026-47892 (WebFlux.fn functional-endpoint header-predicate bypass) and CVE-2026-47893 (WebFlux HandshakeWebSocketService header leak): both require spring-webflux, which does not resolve on the classpath of izgw-hub, izgw-transform, izgw-core, or v2tofhir — verified independently in all four.
Flags on spring-core-6.2.19.jar despite webflux being absent because NVD tracks Spring Framework as one CPE product across all modules, not per-artifact — any module-specific CVE at this version matches every Spring jar we have, including spring-core. A Maven <exclusion> can't fix this: it's a version-string match, not a real transitive dependency, and spring-core itself is required by the framework regardless.
No fix exists on the Spring Framework 6.2.x line; the real fix ships only in 7.0.9, which requires Spring Boot 4.x. Should clear once the Boot 4 upgrade lands. Expires 2027-02-28. Added: 2026-09-02

CVE-2026-47890 (SSE + view-fragment CRLF injection), CVE-2026-47891 (WebFlux + Aalto XML unbounded allocation), and CVE-2026-59282 (data-binding property-path DoS): verified not reachable in izgw-hub, izgw-transform, izgw-core, or v2tofhir. 47890 — no SSE response is produced anywhere. 47891 — neither spring-webflux nor any aalto artifact resolves. 59282 — all 112 request-mapped handlers across the four repos were enumerated (54 transform, 43 hub, 15 core, 0 v2tofhir); none takes @ModelAttribute or a bare POJO command object, so no user-controlled property path reaches the binder.
NOTE: 59282 is a weaker guarantee than the other two — it rests on current handler shape, not on a missing module. No @InitBinder / setAllowedFields allowlisting exists anywhere, so any new handler taking @ModelAttribute or a bare POJO parameter re-opens it while we stay on 6.2.19. Re-verify before extending this expiry.
Same spring-core CPE-matching caveat as the block above. No fix on the Spring Framework 6.2.x line; the fix ships only in 7.0.9, which requires Spring Boot 4.x. Expires 2027-02-28. Added: 2026-09-04

Temporary applicability exception for four CVEs reported against spring-core-6.2.19.jar. Spring Framework 6.2.19 is affected; this is not a claim that the framework is fixed. The affected spring-web, spring-webmvc, and spring-expression artifacts also resolve, so Dependency-Check's product-level match against spring-core is not itself the rationale.
Independent read-only reviews supplied on 2026-09-10 covered these clean revisions: IZGateway/izgw-hub f256578617cb4da32e13520f6ae5d2d44420a78a IZGateway/izgw-transform f77807c435a3dc884d66fef2ca297b98a262a86f IZGateway/izgw-core 71443b6b4a33eb5ed1fa80c5de30a56a57814003 IZGateway/v2tofhir aa49acfd68a85c236c334260b9ee7f791a4c3890 All four freshly resolved Spring Framework 6.2.19 and Spring Boot 3.5.16. Their selected BOM was 1.16.0-20260910.070543-2; mutable SNAPSHOTs can change the runtime graph without changing these repository revisions.
CVE-2026-47884 (XsltView SSRF/RCE): NOT REACHABLE in all four reviewed scopes. XsltView exists, but no applicable XSLT view/resolver registration or implicit-view request path was found. Hub/Transform/Core handlers use REST or direct SOAP/servlet response handling; v2tofhir supplies no controller or application bootstrap. Boot's default static-resource /** mapping does not establish XSLT view rendering. https://spring.io/security/cve-2026-47884
CVE-2026-47885 (PartEvent multipart size-limit bypass): NOT APPLICABLE in all four. PartEventHttpMessageReader exists in spring-web, but WebFlux and Reactor Flux are absent from the reviewed runtime graphs. No inbound PartEvent handling or triggering codec configuration was found; the supplied HTTP paths are synchronous/servlet-based. https://spring.io/security/cve-2026-47885
CVE-2026-47886 (SpEL power-operator DoS): NOT REACHABLE in all four reviewed scopes. SpEL, arbitrary-precision numeric values, and Camel SpEL in Transform are present. No reviewed request path promotes untrusted input into SpEL expression text. Identified expression sources are annotation metadata and startup configuration; HL7/FHIR parsing and FHIRPath evaluation are not SpEL evaluation. Hub's jwt.test-secret and Transform's spring.database influence expression text through ConditionalOnExpression. These configuration sources MUST remain trusted. https://spring.io/security/cve-2026-47886
CVE-2026-47889 (Jetty Core reactive SameSite omission): NOT APPLICABLE in all four. Adapter classes exist in spring-web, but WebFlux, Reactor, and Jetty server classes are absent. Hub/Transform explicitly select servlet Tomcat; Core customizes servlet Tomcat and v2tofhir starts no server. The Jetty Core reactive adapter is not selected. https://spring.io/security/cve-2026-47889
Scope and accepted limits: the user approved this BOM-scan exception on 2026-09-10 for the reviewed configurations. Live images, task definitions, mounted configuration, external Camel routes, and consumer-provided extensions were not assessed. Production applicability remains unconfirmed. This assumes trusted deployment configuration and no additional code/routes enabling the CVEs' prerequisites. The SHA1 and CVE selectors restrict the artifact and findings, NOT the consuming application. Do not reuse this rationale for unreviewed consumers or configurations. Reassess on changes to runtime dependencies, XSLT views, reactive multipart handling, expression sources/configuration trust, external routes/extensions, or server adapters.
The advisories list 6.2.20 as Enterprise Support Only and 7.0.9 as an OSS fix; the public upgrade path requires the coordinated Spring Boot 4 migration. Expiry or a changed JAR hash intentionally restores these findings. Their scanner scores are >= 7, so either can block dependency-update PR creation and publication. Reassess before extending the exception; do not replace it with a Spring-wide CPE rule. Expires 2027-02-28. Added: 2026-09-10
